methodological_rigor.justification: BRUIN CLL-313 is a global, randomized, open-label phase III trial (NCT05023980) with 282 patients, 1:1 randomization, stratification by IGHV status and Rai stage, and a prespecified IRC-assessed PFS primary endpoint. Sample size and power calculations are explicitly stated (90% power for HR 0.41). Analyses include ITT, INV/IRC dual adjudication, prespecified subgroup analyses, and exposure-adjusted safety (EAIR) appropriate for unequal treatment durations. Limitations (open-label design mitigated by blinded IRC, del(17p) exclusion, immature OS) are clearly acknowledged.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a pivotal phase III RCT in treatment-naïve CLL/SLL directly comparing a non-covalent BTKi (pirtobrutinib) with BendaR. The observed HR of 0.199 for PFS and favorable safety profile establish a new frontline option and have clear guideline and regulatory implications. As an individual RCT, Oxford LoE 1b applies; clinical relevance is high (practice-informing).

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript reports patient flow, randomization, stratification, eligibility, intervention details, primary/secondary endpoints, sensitivity analyses, and a full safety section with AE grading per CTCAE v5.0 — consistent with CONSORT. Trial registration, ethics, and informed consent are explicitly stated. Data availability and a data sharing statement are not visible in the normalized text; many pharma-sponsored trials publish such statements at submission, so this is downgraded to 3.

novelty_literature.justification: The study claims to be the first phase III RCT of a non-covalent BTKi exclusively in treatment-naïve CLL/SLL. This is a meaningful extension of the BRUIN program (phase I/II and CLL-321 in R/R settings) and positions pirtobrutinib as a frontline option. While cBTKis have prior frontline trials, the specific agent, noncovalent mechanism, and direct comparison with BendaR fill a documented gap, though not a paradigm shift.

writing_presentation.justification: Writing is precise and well-structured: clear trial design, explicit statistical methods, results presented with HRs, CIs, and 24-month rates, and a thorough discussion contextualizing results against SEQUOIA, ELEVATE TN, and Alliance A041202. Figures and tables are appropriately signposted, and limitations are balanced and specific.

key_strengths: Pivotal global phase III RCT with 282 patients and prespecified IRC-assessed PFS primary endpoint
Very large treatment effect (IRC PFS HR 0.199; 80.1% risk reduction) consistent across INV assessment and subgroups
OS trend favors pirtobrutinib (HR 0.257) despite 52.9% crossover rate; sensitivity analysis confirms
Favorable safety profile including exposure-adjusted analysis and low rates of atrial fibrillation and grade >=3 bleeding
Rigorous statistical plan with alpha control and stratified analyses
key_concerns: Median follow-up of 28.1 months may underestimate BendaR PFS and OS is immature
Open-label design with INV-assessed secondary endpoints (mitigated by blinded IRC primary)
Data-sharing statement not visible in normalized text
chief_reviewer.rationale: A pivotal, methodologically rigorous phase III RCT with a large and clinically meaningful treatment effect in a common malignancy; scope, design, and findings are consistent with Tier 1 oncology journals such as JCO, NEJM-class venues, or Lancet Oncology, pending final OS maturation.
